title: Lupus views of wolf origins
summary: How wolf-born Garou see their ancestry.

claims.text: Lupus claim wolves were among the first of Gaia’s beasts and were always hunters, made by Gaia as they are now.
They resent being reminded that raccoons and hyenas are distant kin.
Some homids argue the forms follow an evolutionary line from human down to wolf, but cannot then explain the Hispo; others see a guiding intelligence behind the Garou.

title: Lupus and the upright forms
summary: Why wolf-born Garou struggle on two legs.

claims.text: Newly Changed lupus must learn to walk upright, and find it far harder than homids find moving on four legs.

Homids and metis choose forms tactically for each situation; lupus view the forms quite differently, and some elders sneer that homids yield to Gaia’s will while lupus must fight it to take an unnatural shape.

title: Lupus breeding rites
summary: Rites for tracking and shaping wolf litters.

claims.text: The Rite of Birth Time, level one, tells a Garou when a wolf will give birth, so lupus know when to go back and see whether a pup is Garou; homids find the rite disgusting.

The Rite of Pure Breeding, level two, judges whether mating a given wolf will pass on a chosen trait such as a larger litter or Garou heritage: one Gnosis and Intelligence + Primal-Urge at difficulty 7, or 9 for heritage.
A wolf that lacks the capacity for a trait will never breed for it.
Over recent decades some lupus have tried a breeding programme to keep their lines strong.
The Gift finds any body of water within twenty miles on Perception + Survival at difficulty 6.
One or two successes give the direction, three or four the distance, and five reveal whether the water is tainted.

title: Toolstick and Tool Talens
summary: A wooden fetish that becomes any tool.

claims.text: The Toolstick, level 3 and Gnosis 6, is a branch from a tree that turns into any tool, still wooden but as hard as steel, on Intelligence + Repair against its Gnosis.
Tool Talens, Gnosis 3, are nuts, pebbles and bark from the wild, kept fifty to a sack, that become five nails or screws per success when used with it.
